project.name:
## Project Name
The unique identifier for your project.

- Must be unique across all projects
- Used in navigation and reports
- Should be clear and descriptive
- Helps team members identify the project scope
project.description:
## Project Description
Additional details about the project's purpose and scope.

- Optional but recommended
- Helps team members understand project goals
- Can include key objectives or requirements
- Limited to 256 characters
project.icon:
## Project Icon
A visual identifier for your project.

- Helps quickly identify the project in lists and dashboards
- Choose from a variety of predefined icons
- Can be changed at any time
- Appears in project navigation and reports
project.completed:
## Project Status
Indicates whether the project is active or completed.

- Active projects are available for testing and updates
- Completed projects are read-only
- Affects project visibility in dashboards
- Can be reversed if needed
project.completedAt:
## Completion Date
The date when the project was marked as completed.

- Automatically set when marking a project as completed
- Used for reporting and tracking
- Helps maintain project history
- Can be modified if needed
project.defaultAccess:
## Default Project Access
Define the default access permissions for users and groups in this project. This can be overridden on a per-user or per-group basis.
project.issueTracker:
## Issue Tracker Configuration
Select the issue tracker configuration to be used for managing issues related to this project.

integrations.externalProjectHelp:
## External Project
Select the project or repository in the external system to link with this TestPlanIt project.

- Issues created from TestPlanIt will be created in this project
- Enables issue tracking integration between systems
- Must have appropriate permissions in the external system
integrations.defaultIssueTypeHelp:
## Default Issue Type
The issue type that will be pre-selected when creating new issues from TestPlanIt.

- Saves time by defaulting to your most common issue type
- Can be overridden when creating individual issues
- Must be a valid issue type for the selected external project
- Update this if your workflow changes
integrations.automaticSyncHelp:
## Automatic Sync
Enables automatic synchronization of issue status between TestPlanIt and the external system.

- Issues linked to test cases will update their status automatically
- Helps keep issue tracking consistent across systems
- May increase API usage with the external service
- Can be disabled if manual control is preferred

user.name:
## User Name
The full name of the user.

- Used for identification across the system
- Displayed in assignments and reports
- Must be unique for each user
user.email:
## Email Address
The user's email address for account access.

- Used for system login
- Must be unique for each user
- Used for system notifications
user.password:
## Password
The user's account password.

- Optional when a passwordless login method is configured (Magic Link SSO provider or email server) — leave blank to require sign-in via magic link or SSO
- When supplied, must satisfy the password policy set in **Admin → Security** (minimum length and character classes)
- Used for secure account access
- Should be kept confidential
user.token:
## Verification Token
Enter the token you received in your email to verify your account. If you don't have a token, you can request a new one.
user.confirmPassword:
## Confirm Password
Re-enter the password to ensure it was typed correctly.

- Must match the password exactly

## Integration Name
A descriptive label for this LLM integration.

- Used to identify it in lists and settings
- Example: "OpenAI GPT-4o" or "Internal Ollama"
llm.provider:
## Provider
The LLM service that powers this integration.

- Determines the API protocol and available models
- Cannot be changed after creation
llm.apiKey:
## API Key
Your authentication key for the LLM provider's API.

- Obtain this from your provider's developer console
- Kept encrypted and never displayed after saving
- Not required for Ollama (local deployment)
llm.endpoint:
## API Endpoint
The base URL for the LLM provider's API.

- Leave blank for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini — official URLs are used automatically
- Required for Ollama (e.g. `http://localhost:11434`), Azure OpenAI, and Custom LLM
- Optional for any provider — point at an OpenAI-compatible proxy (e.g., LiteLLM) by entering its URL
- **Private/internal addresses** (localhost, 127.0.0.1, private IPs, cloud metadata) are blocked unless explicitly allowed via the `ALLOWED_PRIVATE_HOSTS` environment variable
llm.deploymentName:
## Azure Deployment Name
The name of your Azure OpenAI model deployment.

- Found in Azure OpenAI Studio under Deployments
- Different from the model name — e.g. `my-gpt4-deploy` maps to `gpt-4`
- Required only for Azure OpenAI
llm.defaultModel:
## Default Model
The model used for AI requests with this integration.

- For OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini — available models are fetched automatically from your API key
- Ensure the model is enabled in your provider account
- Example: `gpt-4o`, `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `gemini-1.5-pro`
llm.maxTokensPerRequest:
## Max Tokens Per Request
The **hard ceiling** on output tokens for any single request.

- Requests exceeding this are **rejected with an error** before reaching the LLM
- Set this to your model's actual maximum output token capacity
- Example: `16384` for GPT-4o, `8192` for Claude 3.5 Sonnet
- Setting this too low causes AI features to fail or produce truncated output
llm.defaultMaxTokens:
## Default Max Tokens
The **fallback** output token limit used when a request doesn't specify its own.

- Each AI feature (test generation, code export, etc.) sets its own limit in **Admin → Prompt Config**
- This value is only used as a fallback for features with no specific limit configured
- Should be ≤ Max Tokens Per Request
llm.maxRequestsPerMinute:
## Max Requests Per Minute
Limits how many API calls can be made to this provider per minute.

- Set to match your provider plan's rate limit
- Excess requests are queued, not rejected
- Check your provider's documentation for your plan's limit
llm.costPerInputToken:
## Cost Per Input Token (USD)
The cost in USD for each input (prompt) token sent to the model.

- Used for cost tracking and budget alerts
- Find this on your provider's pricing page
- Example: `0.000005` = $5 per million input tokens
llm.costPerOutputToken:
## Cost Per Output Token (USD)
The cost in USD for each output (completion) token generated by the model.

- Usually higher than the input token cost
- Used for cost tracking and budget alerts
- Example: `0.000015` = $15 per million output tokens
llm.monthlyBudget:
## Monthly Budget (USD)
An optional spending target for this integration.

- Set to `0` to disable budget tracking
- Budget is **informational only** — it does not block LLM usage
- You'll receive notifications at 80%, 90%, and 100% of the budget
- Costs are calculated using the per-token rates above
llm.billingPeriodStartDay:
## Billing Period Start Day
The day of month (1–31) when your billing period starts.

- Default `1` aligns with the calendar month
- Set to `15` for a 15th-to-15th cycle (e.g., to match your provider invoice date)
- Values `29–31` automatically clamp to the last day of shorter months (Feb in non-leap years, etc.)
- Affects the **Monthly Budget** spend window and the **Reset Spend** action
llm.defaultTemperature:
## Default Temperature
Controls the randomness of model responses (0–2).

- **0:** Deterministic — identical output for the same input
- **0.3:** Focused — recommended for test generation and code output
- **1+:** Creative — more varied responses
- Individual features can override this in Prompt Config
llm.timeout:
## Request Timeout (ms)
How long to wait for a response before the request is cancelled.

- Value is in milliseconds (e.g. `30000` = 30 seconds)
- Streaming requests (e.g. code export preview) ignore this timeout
- Increase for slow or large models
- Range: 5,000 – 600,000 ms
llm.streamingEnabled:
## Enable Streaming
Streams the response token-by-token instead of waiting for the full output.

- Required for real-time code preview in the Export modal
- Reduces perceived latency for long responses
- Recommended for all supported providers

- Features without a specific provider configured will use the default
- Can be changed at any time

caseField.displayName:
## Display Name
This is the human-readable name for the field that will be shown to users in forms and views. Make it clear and descriptive.
caseField.systemName:
## System Name
A unique identifier for this field used internally by the system (e.g., in API calls, database queries). It will be auto-generated from the Display Name but can be customized. Must start with a letter. Can only contain letters, numbers, and underscores (no spaces or special characters).
caseField.hint:
## Hint Text (Optional)
Provide a short instruction or example that will appear below the field to guide users. This can clarify expected input or formatting.
caseField.enabled:
## Enabled
Determines if this field is active and available for use in templates and test cases. Disabled fields are hidden and their data is preserved but not used.
caseField.required:
## Required
If checked, users must provide a value for this field when creating or editing a test case using a template that includes this field.
caseField.restricted:
## Restricted
If checked, only users with special permissions (e.g., Super Admins or those with 'Case Restricted Fields' permission) can edit this field's value once a case is created. Other users will see it as read-only. This is useful for fields like 'Reviewed By' or 'Approved Date' that should not be changed by general users after a certain stage.
caseField.fieldType:
## Field Type
Determines the kind of data this field will store and how it will be displayed (e.g., Text, Number, Date, Dropdown). The field type cannot be changed after creation.
caseField.defaultValue:
## Default Value (Optional)
Set a pre-filled value for this field. For 'Checkbox' type, use 'true' or 'false'. For 'Dropdown' or 'Multi-Select', this usually refers to the ID(s) of the default option(s). For other types, it's the literal default text/number. This can be overridden when the field is added to a template.
caseField.isChecked:
## Default State (for Checkbox)
Determines if the checkbox should be checked by default when a new item (e.g., test case) is being created.
caseField.minValue:
## Minimum Value (for Number/Integer)
Sets the smallest allowed numeric value for this field. Both Min and Max Value must be set if one is used.
caseField.maxValue:
## Maximum Value (for Number/Integer)
Sets the largest allowed numeric value for this field. Both Min and Max Value must be set if one is used.
caseField.initialHeight:
## Initial Height (for Text Long)
Specify the initial display height (in pixels) for rich text editor fields. This helps control the form layout for longer text inputs.
caseField.dropdownOptions:
## Options (for Dropdown/Multi-Select)
Define the list of choices available for selection. You can reorder options, set a default, and enable/disable individual options.

exportModal.scope:
## Export Scope
Determines which test cases will be included in the export:
- **Selected:** Exports only the test cases you have explicitly selected in the table.
- **All Filtered:** Exports all test cases that match the current filter criteria in the table, even if not all are currently visible on the page.
- **All Project:** Exports every test case in the current project, ignoring any selections or filters.
exportModal.format:
## Export Format
Choose the file format for your export.
- **CSV (Comma Separated Values):** A plain text file suitable for spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets) and data analysis tools. PDF export is planned for a future release.
exportModal.columns:
## Columns to Export (CSV Only)
Determines which data columns will be included for each test case:
- **All Columns:** Exports all available data fields for the test cases, including custom fields from their templates.
- **Visible Columns:** Exports only the columns currently visible in the test case table.
exportModal.delimiter:
## CSV Delimiter (CSV Only)
Choose the character used to separate values in the CSV file. The most common is Comma. Use a different delimiter if your data contains commas within text fields (e.g., Semicolon).
exportModal.textLongFormat:
## Long Text Field Format (CSV Only)
Determines how rich text fields (like 'Description' or custom 'Text Long' fields) are exported:
- **JSON:** Exports the content as a JSON string, preserving all formatting (bold, lists, etc.). This is best for re-importing or programmatic processing.
- **Plain Text:** Exports the content as plain text, stripping out formatting. This is more readable in simple text viewers.
exportModal.stepsFormat:
## Steps Format (CSV Only)
Determines how test steps (including expected results) are exported:
- **JSON:** Exports steps as a JSON array of objects, preserving structure and rich text. Suitable for re-import or detailed analysis.
- **Plain Text:** Exports steps in a simplified, readable plain text format, with each step and expected result on a new line.
exportModal.rowMode:
## Row Mode (CSV Only)
Determines how multi-value fields (like Tags or Multi-Select custom fields) and Steps are represented:
- **Single Row per Case:** Each test case is a single row. Multi-value fields and steps will be condensed into their respective cells (often as JSON or concatenated text).
- **Multiple Rows per Case:** A test case can span multiple rows if it has multiple tags, multi-select values, or steps. Each unique value/step for such fields will create a new row, with other case data repeated. This is useful for detailed analysis or pivoting.
exportModal.attachmentFormat:
## Attachment Info Format (CSV Only)
Determines how information about attachments is exported:
- **JSON:** Exports attachment details (like filename, URL, size) as a JSON array. This is comprehensive but less human-readable directly in a CSV.
- **Names Only:** Exports a comma-separated list of attachment filenames. Simpler for quick reference.

codeRepository.name:
## Repository Name
A friendly display name for this repository connection.

- Used to identify it in project code context settings.
- Does not need to match the repository name on the provider.
codeRepository.provider:
## Git Provider
The platform hosting this repository.

- **GitHub** — github.com (cloud or Enterprise)
- **GitLab** — gitlab.com or self-hosted
- **Bitbucket Cloud** — bitbucket.org (cloud only)
- **Azure DevOps** — dev.azure.com
- **Gitea / Forgejo / Gogs** — self-hosted Git servers with compatible APIs
codeRepository.githubToken:
## Personal Access Token
A GitHub token with **Contents: Read** permission.

Generate one at: GitHub → Profile Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens.
codeRepository.owner:
## Owner
The GitHub organization or user account that owns the repository.

- Example: `myorg` or `myusername`
- This is the first path segment in your repository URL on github.com
codeRepository.repo:
## Repository
The repository name, without the owner prefix.

- Example: `my-repo` (not `myorg/my-repo`)
- This is the second path segment in your repository URL on github.com
codeRepository.githubBaseUrl:
## API Base URL
Leave blank for github.com. For GitHub Enterprise Server, enter the full API root.

- Example: `https://github.example.com/api/v3`
- Typically ends in `/api/v3`
- Must be reachable from this server
codeRepository.gitlabToken:
## Personal Access Token
A GitLab token with **read_api** and **read_repository** scopes.

Generate one at: GitLab → User Settings → Access Tokens.
codeRepository.projectPath:
## Project ID or Path
The numeric project ID or full namespace path.

- Example path: `myorg/my-project`
- Example ID: `12345678`
- Found in GitLab under Settings → General.
codeRepository.baseUrl:
## GitLab URL
Leave blank for gitlab.com. For self-hosted instances, enter your GitLab URL.

- Example: `https://gitlab.example.com`
codeRepository.bitbucketEmail:
## Atlassian Account Email
The email address associated with your Atlassian account.

- This is the email you use to log in to Bitbucket Cloud.
codeRepository.bitbucketApiToken:
## API Token
A Bitbucket API token with **Repositories: Read** scope.

Create one at: Bitbucket → Personal settings → API tokens.

> App passwords have been deprecated by Atlassian in favor of API tokens.
codeRepository.workspace:
## Workspace
The workspace slug from your Bitbucket URL.

- Example: `myworkspace` from `bitbucket.org/myworkspace`
codeRepository.repoSlug:
## Repository Slug
The repository identifier from its URL.

- Example: `my-repo` from `bitbucket.org/myworkspace/my-repo`
codeRepository.azureToken:
## Personal Access Token
An Azure DevOps PAT with **Code (Read)** permission.

Create one at: Azure DevOps → User settings → Personal access tokens.
codeRepository.organizationUrl:
## Organization URL
Your Azure DevOps organization URL.

- Example: `https://dev.azure.com/myorg`
codeRepository.project:
## Project Name
The name of the Azure DevOps project containing the repository.

- Found as the third path segment in your Azure DevOps URL after the organization name
codeRepository.azureRepoId:
## Repository Name or ID
The repository name or GUID within the Azure DevOps project.

- Example: `my-repo`
codeRepository.giteaToken:
## Personal Access Token
A token with repository read permissions.

Generate one at: Site Administration → Applications, or User Settings → Applications.

- Works with Gitea, Forgejo, Gogs, and any server exposing a compatible API.
codeRepository.giteaBaseUrl:
## Server URL
The base URL of your self-hosted Git server.

- Example: `https://gitea.example.com`
- Must include the protocol (https:// recommended)
- Works with Gitea, Forgejo, Gogs, and other servers with a Gitea-compatible `/api/v1/` REST API
codeRepository.giteaOwner:
## Owner
The organization or user account that owns the repository.

- Example: `myorg` or `myusername`
- This is the first path segment in your repository URL
codeRepository.giteaRepo:
## Repository
The repository name, without the owner prefix.

- Example: `my-repo` (not `myorg/my-repo`)

promptConfig.name:
## Configuration Name
A unique, descriptive name for this prompt configuration.

- Used to identify the configuration when assigning it to a project (e.g. "GPT-4o Prompts", "Conservative Prompts").
promptConfig.description:
## Description
An optional summary of what makes this configuration distinct.

- Helps admins understand the purpose at a glance (e.g. "Lower temperature prompts for deterministic output").
promptConfig.isActive:
## Active
When enabled, this configuration is available for use by projects.

- Inactive configurations are hidden from project assignment dropdowns.
- The default configuration cannot be deactivated.
promptConfig.isDefault:
## Default Configuration
When enabled, this configuration is used by any project that has not been assigned a specific configuration.

- Only one configuration can be the default at a time.
- Setting a new default automatically unsets the previous one.
promptConfig.systemPrompt:
## System Prompt
Instructions sent to the AI model before any user input. Defines the model's role, output format, and constraints.

- Supports double-brace placeholders (e.g. FRAMEWORK, LANGUAGE, CASE_NAME) that are substituted at runtime.
- Changes here affect every project using this configuration.
promptConfig.userPrompt:
## User Prompt
The message sent to the AI on behalf of the user. Leave blank if the feature constructs the user message entirely in code.

- Supports double-brace placeholders (e.g. ISSUE_TITLE, CASE_NAME, CODE_CONTEXT) that are substituted at runtime.
- The available placeholders for each feature are listed in the Variables section below.
promptConfig.temperature:
## Temperature
Controls the randomness of the AI output. Range: 0–2.

- **0.0–0.3** — Highly deterministic, best for structured output (JSON, code).
- **0.4–0.7** — Balanced, good for test case generation.
- **0.8–2.0** — More creative and varied, suitable for open-ended text.
promptConfig.maxOutputTokens:
## Max Output Tokens
The maximum number of tokens the model will generate in a single response.

- Higher values allow longer responses but increase cost and latency.
- Typical ranges: 2048 for short text, 4096 for code generation, 6000+ for multi-case output.

automationCandidates.casesToRankHelp: How many manual test cases to send to the LLM for ranking. Higher numbers give broader coverage but the LLM takes proportionally longer (range: 5–100; thinking models can run several minutes at the top end).
automationCandidates.selectionStrategyHelp: Which strategy decides which manual cases to send when the project has more than the per-generation cap. **Most Executed** (default) picks the cases that have been run the most across test runs — best ROI for automation. **Flakiest First** picks cases whose pass/fail outcomes flip the most — prime candidates for a deterministic automation oracle. **Longest to Execute** picks the cases with the highest manual-execution forecast (tester-derived; falls back to the original estimate) — automation directly recovers the most tester time. **Oldest First** picks long-lived manual cases (stable, mature). **Newest First** picks the most-recently created cases. **Random** is an unbiased sample. Only manual cases whose workflow state is *In Progress* or *Done* are eligible.

Configure an LLM integration (Admin → AI Models) to enable richer reasoning that weighs custom fields, linked-issue context, and case content alongside the metric.

strategyExplanation.most_executed: Cases are ordered by manual-execution count (highest first) — the regression-frequency proxy where automation directly recovers the most tester time.
strategyExplanation.flakiest_first: Cases are ordered by approximate flakiness (pass/fail flips) — flaky manual tests are prime candidates for a deterministic automation oracle.
strategyExplanation.longest_first: Cases are ordered by manual-execution forecast (longest first; forecastManual when present, falls back to estimate) — automation recovers the most tester time on these.
strategyExplanation.oldest_first: Cases are ordered by creation date (oldest first) — long-lived manual cases tend to be mature, stable behaviors that are safe to automate without rework.
strategyExplanation.newest_first: Cases are ordered by creation date (newest first) — newly-authored cases are the most likely to need execution coverage right now.
strategyExplanation.random: Cases are an unbiased random sample of the eligible set.

rationale.flakiestNone: No varied outcomes yet — the Flakiest First heuristic can't yet measure pass/fail flipping for this case.
rationale.longestWithDuration: Manual-execution forecast {duration} — automating long-running manual tests recovers proportionally more tester time on every run.
rationale.longestNone: No forecast or estimate set — the Longest to Execute heuristic has no duration data for this case.
rationale.oldest: Authored {age} — long-lived manual cases tend to be mature, stable behaviors that are safe to automate without rework.
rationale.newest: Authored {age} — newly-authored cases are the most likely to need execution coverage right now.
rationale.random: Random sample — included as an unbiased reference; the heuristic mode has no inherent preference for this case over the others in the sample.
